title: One-hot EX forwarding bypass
motivation: The reported worst path starts at a MEM/WB destination register and passes through forwarding and the EX ALU. The current design encodes forwarding priority into a two-bit select and then decodes it through a separate operand mux, adding selection depth before the ALU.

hypothesis.motivation: The reported worst path starts at a MEM/WB destination register and passes through forwarding and the EX ALU. The current design encodes forwarding priority into a two-bit select and then decodes it through a separate operand mux, adding selection depth before the ALU.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Express EX/MEM, MEM/WB, and register-file forwarding as priority-qualified one-hot grants, and form each forwarded operand with masked data terms combined by OR. This should remove the encoded-select decode from the forwarding-to-ALU path while preserving youngest-writer priority and x0 behavior, improving Fmax on the observed critical path.

title: Iterative divider removes the long ALU path
motivation: The measured worst path starts in the MEM/WB destination register and runs through forwarding and EX/ALU logic before reaching the data-memory address. The current combinational DIV and REM operators add a deep arithmetic cone to this shared execution path, even though CoreMark is expected to use division infrequently.

hypothesis.motivation: The measured worst path starts in the MEM/WB destination register and runs through forwarding and EX/ALU logic before reaching the data-memory address. The current combinational DIV and REM operators add a deep arithmetic cone to this shared execution path, even though CoreMark is expected to use division infrequently.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Replace the combinational DIV/REM operators with one shared radix-2 iterative divider that computes quotient and remainder over multiple cycles, handling signedness and the RISC-V divide corner cases. Hold the current instruction in ID/EX while the divider runs, let older instructions drain through MEM/WB, and release the pipeline when the result is ready. Removing the combinational divider should shorten the critical arithmetic path and raise Fmax, while the added latency affects only divide and remainder instructions.

implementation_notes:
# Implementation notes

## Changes

- Removed the real combinational DIV/REM `/` and `%` operators from the ALU.
- Added `rtl/divider.sv`, a shared radix-2 restoring divider. Normal operations
  take 32 cycles; divide-by-zero and signed overflow return their RISC-V defined
  values directly.
- EX holds a DIV/REM instruction in ID/EX, inserts EX/MEM bubbles while it
  runs, and releases the pipeline when the result is ready. Older instructions
  continue through MEM/WB. The forwarded source operands are saved at divider
  start for correct RVFI reporting after the forwarding sources have drained.
- Added divider vectors for signed and unsigned quotient/remainder, zero
  divisors, signed overflow, and repeated operations. Removed division vectors
  from the combinational ALU suite.

## Deviations and concerns

- `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` keeps its existing combinational ALU substitutions and
  bypasses divider waiting. This preserves the fast bounded formal model; the
  hardware divider is exercised by its unit tests and cosimulation instead.
- The normal divider latency is 32 cycles. Only DIV/REM instructions incur
  this delay.

## Local checks

- Verilator lint: passed with the requested `-Wall` command.
- ALU and divider cocotb tests: 2 pytest entries passed.
- Formal: 53 passed, 0 failed using the nret=1 wrapper and checks. An initial
  run under the shared `bench` staging name collided with another formal
  workdir and ended as `no_checks_generated`; rerunning with an isolated core
  name completed successfully.
- Cosimulation: passed both selftest and CoreMark ELFs with `NRET=1`, including
  the stall scenarios and CoreMark checks.
- Gowin timing, placement option 0: 45.327 MHz. The new worst path runs from a
  register-file bit through ID/EX; it does not cross the divider.
lesson: - 2026-09-28 hyp-20260928-002-r1s1 (improvement, +689.27%): Moving DIV/REM out of the shared combinational ALU path into a 32-cycle iterative unit raised Fmax sharply; holding ID/EX while bubbling EX/MEM lets infrequent CoreMark divides pay latency without keeping division on every instruction’s critical path.

title: Predict backward branches in fetch
motivation: The five-stage core currently resolves every conditional branch and jump in EX, then redirects fetch and flushes younger work even when the branch is a recurring loop back-edge. CoreMark contains many loop back-edges, so their repeated redirect bubbles reduce useful instructions per cycle.

hypothesis.motivation: The five-stage core currently resolves every conditional branch and jump in EX, then redirects fetch and flushes younger work even when the branch is a recurring loop back-edge. CoreMark contains many loop back-edges, so their repeated redirect bubbles reduce useful instructions per cycle.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a fetch-stage static BTFNT predictor: predict aligned backward conditional branches taken, forward branches not taken, and aligned direct JAL instructions taken. Carry the predicted next PC with each instruction and redirect from EX only when the resolved branch or jump's actual next PC differs. This should remove the repeated EX redirect penalty from correctly predicted loops and direct jumps while preserving recovery for mispredictions.

title: Narrow ID flush to control state
motivation: After removing the combinational divider, the measured critical path runs from a register-file value through EX control, fetch redirect, hazard logic, and back to ID, ending at an ID/EX operand register. The current ID flush clears the entire packed pipeline register, so the branch redirect and hazard path controls a wide mux on every payload bit, including the source operands.

hypothesis.motivation: After removing the combinational divider, the measured critical path runs from a register-file value through EX control, fetch redirect, hazard logic, and back to ID, ending at an ID/EX operand register. The current ID flush clears the entire packed pipeline register, so the branch redirect and hazard path controls a wide mux on every payload bit, including the source operands.
hypothesis.hypothesis: On an ID flush, clear only the ID/EX control bundle and valid bit while retaining the prior data payload; continue to clear the full register on reset and load the full payload on normal capture. With valid low and controls zero, the retained PC, instruction, operands, and destination are inert, while flush no longer selects zero across the wide operand and metadata registers. This should remove the branch-redirect/hazard control signal from the critical operand-register input path.

changes.description: On flush, invalidate the ID/EX entry and clear its controls without clearing the wide data payload, removing flush control from operand-register inputs while preserving bubble side-effect safety.

title: Banked one-hot register-file reads
motivation: The current worst path begins in the register file and ends at an ID/EX operand register, so the asynchronous 32-entry read selection is on the measured clock path. Restructuring both read ports can shorten this path without adding an instruction stage or changing retirement behavior.

hypothesis.motivation: The current worst path begins in the register file and ends at an ID/EX operand register, so the asynchronous 32-entry read selection is on the measured clock path. Restructuring both read ports can shorten this path without adding an instruction stage or changing retirement behavior.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Organize the register file as four banks of eight words and use shared address predecode with parallel local word selection and bank selection for each read port, rather than relying on a single variable-index array read. Preserve x0, synchronous writes, reset-to-zero, and the same-cycle write-first bypass. The factored read network should map into shallower FPGA LUT logic, improving Fmax on the present register-file-to-ID critical path while retaining one-instruction-per-cycle throughput.

changes.description: Replace the variable-index asynchronous reads with a four-bank, predecoded hierarchical read structure for both operands while preserving write, reset, x0, and bypass semantics.

lesson: - 2026-09-28 hyp-20260928-002-r2s1 (regression, +8.73%): Banking a flop-based register file with explicit one-hot AND/OR selection can regress FPGA fitness because duplicated wide read reductions and per-word write decoding may cost more than the indexed mux they replace.

title: Predict function returns with a small RAS
motivation: The prior static BTFNT predictor regressed because its fetch path decoded branch immediates and added target logic. Function returns are also frequent control transfers in CoreMark, and their targets are already available from recent call return addresses. Predicting only canonical JALR returns can remove their EX redirect bubbles without adding a branch-immediate adder to fetch.

hypothesis.motivation: The prior static BTFNT predictor regressed because its fetch path decoded branch immediates and added target logic. Function returns are also frequent control transfers in CoreMark, and their targets are already available from recent call return addresses. Predicting only canonical JALR returns can remove their EX redirect bubbles without adding a branch-immediate adder to fetch.
hypothesis.hypothesis: Add a four-entry return-address stack. Push pc+4 when a valid JAL or JALR writes the link register x1 or x5, and recognize canonical returns (JALR x0, 0(x1/x5)) in fetch to select the stack top as the predicted next PC. Carry the prediction with the instruction and have EX redirect only when the resolved next PC differs, preserving the existing recovery path for incorrect or unavailable predictions. Keep all target arithmetic out of fetch; its new work is a narrow instruction check and a small stack-top mux.
